svg.aria-label: A neighbour solicitation sent to a solicited-node multicast group that only the router has joined, and the router's neighbour advertisement in reply

g.text: to ff02::1:ff40:b32, in a frame to 33:33:ff:40:0b:32
not in that group: its card ignores the frame

ol.li: Bob’s MacBook wants the router’s card address. IPv6 has no broadcast, so instead of shouting at everyone (Chapter 21’s ARP), it sends an ICMPv6 neighbour solicitation to a “solicited-node” multicast group, made from the last 24 bits of the address it’s looking for. Only a device whose address ends that way has joined that group, so the other cards throw the frame away without even bothering the computer.

The router sends back a neighbour advertisement with its card address, and the flags “I’m a router” and “this is an answer”. Both messages are real, from Bob’s network, and this chapter’s lab can show you yours. (The phone’s address has been changed.)

figure.figcaption: Neighbour discovery: ARP’s job, done with ICMPv6 and multicast.
